_CORRECTION_NOTICE_2026-09-13: CRITICAL: every entry in this file (method_renames, reshaped_families, simple_families, per_zone_id_file_conventions.shape_C_zones_table_global, script_shape's SOL_REGISTER-style examples) was checked against D:\Claude\landsandboat-reference (LandSandBoat/server, a MODERN sol2-based fork) -- but the real production target ('Valhalla') actually runs D:\Claude\old-dsp-reference (DarkstarProject/darkstar, last commit 2017-10-22, an OLDER Lunar-binding-style codebase that predates even Topaz's own tpz.* namespace tables). These are NOT the same codebase. See D:\Claude\Topaz-Assault-Backport\reports\old_dsp_reference_correction_2026-09-13.md for the full corrected binding-by-binding table. Every entry below is real research and stays valid IF this project ever targets LandSandBoat -- but treat it as 'checked_against: landsandboat-reference (NOT this project's real target)' unless a given entry has been explicitly re-confirmed against old-dsp-reference and marked so. KEY OLD-DSP-REFERENCE FACTS CONFIRMED 2026-09-13 (grep-verified against the real checkout): (1) binding registration uses LUNAR_DECLARE_METHOD(CLuaBaseEntity,X) in src/map/lua/lua_baseentity.cpp (no underscore in filename), not SOL_REGISTER; (2) getShortID, SetAutoAttackEnabled, untargetable all exist in old-dsp-reference under Topaz's OWN exact spelling -- the landsandboat-based renames to getTargID/setAutoAttackEnabled/setUntargetable are WRONG for the real target and were reverted; (3) old-dsp-reference has NO setName, NO goToEntity/gotoEntity (only gotoPlayer), NO setSpeed/setBaseSpeed (only a unified 'speed' method), NO isAggroable/setIsAggroable Lua binding, and NO checkNavPath/checkNavPosition/isNavigablePoint binding anywhere in src/map/lua/*.cpp -- these are real gaps needing further investigation/C++ work, not simple renames; (4) old-dsp-reference does NOT even use a tpz.* or xi.* namespace table for most constant families (e.g. MOD_DEF is a bare global, not tpz.mod.DEF or xi.mod.DEF) -- this is a MUCH older convention than either Topaz's current tpz.* or LandSandBoat's xi.*, and most of this file's family mappings need re-verification against that fact; (5) GM commands use bare `cmdprops`/`onTrigger` globals (matching Topaz's own convention exactly, confirmed via src/map/commandhandler.cpp's lua_getglobal(m_LState,"cmdprops")), NOT LandSandBoat's commandObj-wrapper shape; (6) zone id files in old-dsp-reference are inconsistent per-zone: Periqia/Lebros_Cavern/Leujaoam_Sanctum have a real IDs.lua with a bare capitalized-but-SHORTENED global table name (Periqia, Lebros, Leujaoam -- not the full folder name), consumed via `local ID = zones[xi.zone.X]` in the WRONG (landsandboat) conversion and corrected to `local ID = <BareName>` directly (no zones[] indirection at all in old-dsp-reference) -- while Ilrusi_Atoll, Mamool_Ja_Training_Grounds, and Aht_Urhgan_Whitegate instead use a split TextIDs.lua/MobIDs.lua convention with NO consolidated IDs.lua at all, which has NOT yet been fully re-converted (flagged as remaining work).
_readme: Confirmed Topaz(tpz.*) -> DSP(darkstar-cd74c6d43c3d219b41490512f74a30b866e818a0) namespace mappings. Each entry was verified against real DSP source (not guessed from a general pattern) -- see 'source' and 'evidence' fields. 'confidence' is 'confirmed' (numeric/behavioral match checked), 'confirmed_pattern' (2+ spot-checked values matched, rest inferred safe), or 'engine_gap' (does not exist in DSP, needs a C++ addition before Lua can use it -- never auto-convert these). Regenerate/extend this file every time a new zone package surfaces a family not yet covered here -- don't re-derive from scratch, and don't guess a mapping without checking real DSP source the way every entry here was checked.

simple_families._readme: shape: 'tpz.<family>.<KEY>' -> '<dsp_prefix><KEY>' (or a lookup in 'renames' for keys whose NAME differs, not just the prefix). Safe for the converter to auto-apply.

effect.evidence: 17 values spot-checked, all exact matches (STUN=10, DEBILITATION=263, OMERTA=262, etc). A separate SUBEFFECT_* family exists in the same file -- confirmed unrelated (proc/message category, not status effect id) -- never use it for tpz.effect.*.

effectFlag.evidence: DISPELABLE=0x0001, ERASABLE=0x0002 exact match, actively used in ~15 real DSP scripts. INFLUENCE/OFFLINE_TICK/AURA/EMPATHY were all confirmed missing (backport_map_confidence_check.py full-usage sweep) and RESOLVED 2026-09-13 -- see engine_gaps.effectFlag_INFLUENCE, now ported. ON_ZONE_PATHOS is a dead reference even in Topaz's own source -- never appears in real code, comment-only, no action needed.

mod.evidence: MOD_FIRE_ABSORB=459, MOD_DARK_ABSORB=466 exact match for the elemental *_ABSORB family; other tpz.mod.* members not individually re-checked, verify before relying on an unconfirmed one. KNOWN LARGE DECAY AREA (backport_map_confidence_check.py full-usage sweep, 2026-09-12): of 469 real tpz.mod.* members used anywhere in Topaz, 69 (~15%) have no MOD_<name> identifier anywhere in this DSP snapshot at all -- this DSP checkout's MOD_ enum is simply older/smaller than modern Topaz's, missing many newer roll/augment/job-trait modifiers (e.g. PHANTOM_ROLL, DESPOIL, FAST_CAST, most WS_<STAT>_BONUS entries). NOT individually engine_gap'd member-by-member (69 entries is too many to usefully enumerate here) -- treat any tpz.mod.* reference in a real conversion as needing an explicit per-member check against this DSP snapshot's mod.h/status.lua before trusting the blind prefix rule, rather than assuming the pattern holds. Re-run backport_map_confidence_check.py --family mod for the current full list.

path_flag.evidence: PATHFLAG_NONE=0, RUN=1, WALLHACK=2, REVERSE=4 exact match. DSP additionally HAS a PATHFLAG_SCRIPT=8 and PATHFLAG_SLIDE=0x10 that Topaz's own tpz.path.flag table (as shipped in this Topaz checkout) does NOT define at all -- confirmed real, currently-live bug in Ilrusi_Atoll/npcs/QiqirnDiver_Common.lua referencing tpz.path.flag.SCRIPT (which is nil in Topaz, throwing on every pathTo() call using it -- see [[topaz_pathto_wallhack_default]] memory). reshaped_families._readme: shape differs from a simple prefix swap -- table nesting added/removed, or the table name itself changes. Each needs its own substitution rule, not a blind prefix replace.

job.evidence: JOBS.COR, JOBS.THF used live -- a table like Topaz's own tpz.job, NOT a bare JOBTYPE_WAR global the general prefix pattern would suggest. Rule: tpz.job.X -> JOBS.X (drop tpz., keep the two-level shape).

magic_ele.evidence: ELE_FIRE=1 exact match. Rule: tpz.magic.ele.X -> ELE_X (flatten, drop nesting).

teleport.evidence: TELEPORT_ESCAPE=8 exact match. Rule: tpz.teleport.X (a type CONSTANT, not the table's other fields like .to/.id/.type) -> TELEPORT_X, bare. The whole globals/teleports.lua calling convention differs beyond this one value -- read both files side by side before porting any script that builds a tpz.teleport{} call table.

nyzul.source: n/a -- tpz.nyzul is Topaz's own bespoke module, DSP has no Nyzul Isle Investigation implementation to match against
nyzul.evidence: Design decision, not a discovery: renamed to a capitalized bare-global table `Nyzul` matching DSP's own convention for shared utility modules (npcUtil, chatType, msgBasic all follow this bare-capitalized-table shape). Rule: tpz.nyzul.X -> Nyzul.X. Applies to globals/nyzul.lua and globals/nyzul/*.lua's own internal cross-references too, not just call sites in mob/npc/instance scripts. If a future package introduces its own bespoke Topaz-only module (not present in DSP at all), add it here the same way -- pick a bare-capitalized name, document it as 'our_own_convention', don't leave it unmapped.

instance_updateInstanceTime.evidence: DSP already ships a complete, working updateInstanceTime(instance, elapsed, texttable) as a bare global function -- identical signature to Topaz's tpz.instance.updateInstanceTime. Rule: drop the ENTIRE tpz.instance. prefix (not just tpz.), call bare. Do not port globals/instance.lua's Topaz version -- DSP's own already does the job.

msg_basic.evidence: msgBasic.REQUIRES_A_PET=215, msgBasic.DISAPPEAR_NUM=231 exact match. msgBasic.NO_EFFECT=189 matches tpz.msg.basic.SKILL_NO_EFFECT (name differs). DSP's msgBasic table is a smaller subset of Topaz's -- a value used in Topaz may need a NEW line added to DSP's own msg.lua (pure data, e.g. 'RECOVERS_HP = 24,') rather than an existing name to map to. Check every key individually with grep before assuming it exists.

anim_table.source: landsandboat-reference/scripts/commands/animatenpc.lua (DSP's own real, native file), which does animationId = tonumber(animationId) or xi.anim[string.upper(animationId)]
anim_table.evidence: Direct table rename, same [KEY] dynamic-lookup shape as Topaz's tpz.anim -- confirmed by reading DSP's own native animatenpc.lua rather than guessing. Rule: tpz.anim -> xi.anim (bare table reference, not a per-key rename since callers index it dynamically with string.upper(arg), not a fixed named key).

incompatible_enums._readme: A DSP family with the SAME general shape as a Topaz one but INCOMPATIBLE VALUES past a partial overlap -- converting by number instead of by name silently corrupts behavior. Never numeric-map these; always name-map via the explicit table.

damage_type_family.warning: tpz.attackType.MAGICAL(=2) vs MOBSKILL_MAGICAL(=1): DSP has no NONE=0 slot, entire enum is offset by one from Topaz's. tpz.damageType.FIRE(=6) coincidentally equals MOBPARAM_FIRE(=6), but LIGHTNING(=10 in Topaz) would silently become DSP's own ICE(=10) if ported by number -- confirmed by tracing a real DSP mobskill (10000_needles.lua). The PHYSICAL half of damageType (PIERCING/SLASHING/BLUNT/HTH) was found missing from this map entirely during the outside-Nyzul stress test (Lebros_Cavern/mobs/Qiqirn_Mine.lua uses tpz.attackType.PHYSICAL/tpz.damageType.NONE) -- DSP's physical MOBPARAM_* names don't even share Topaz's spelling (SLASH not SLASHING, PIERCE not PIERCING, H2H not HTH), confirmed against scripts/globals/monstertpmoves.lua. tpz.damageType.ELEMENTAL(=5, a generic/unused Topaz value per its own source comment) has NO DSP equivalent at all -- if a real call site ever uses it (none found yet in any zone checked), treat as a new engine_gap rather than guessing a mapping. ALWAYS use the name_map above, never the numeric value.
damage_type_family.call_convention_change: target:takeDamage(dmg, mob, attackType, damageType) does not exist in DSP -- rewrite as: local dmg = MobFinalAdjustments(rawDmg, mob, skill, target, MOBSKILL_X, MOBPARAM_Y, shadowbehav); target:delHP(dmg)

mission_tracking.note: DSP's own scripts/globals/log_ids.lua + missions.lua implement mission tracking with a DIFFERENT calling convention than Topaz's tpz.mission.* tables -- DSP's nation/log argument (e.g. TOAU) is a whole table object ({mission_log=4,...}), not Topaz's bare int. Where DSP already has a working script for the same mechanic (e.g. Nyzul's own _20m.lua entry-gating), prefer diffing against DSP's existing file for genuinely new content rather than porting Topaz's rewritten version wholesale.

Rytaal.note: The real NPC that dispenses IMPERIAL_ARMY_ID_TAG (daily id_tags currency, up to 3 banked) -- a load-bearing dependency for EVERY Assault zone's mission giver (Sorrowful_Sage.lua and its 5 siblings all gate on player:hasKeyItem(IMPERIAL_ARMY_ID_TAG)), not Nyzul-specific. DSP's own copy is a complete, working, non-stub implementation (unlike Sorrowful_Sage.lua's original disabled-stub state) -- its onEventFinish already explicitly checks for and consumes NYZUL_ISLE_ASSAULT_ORDERS by name alongside the other 5 zones' order key items, meaning it already natively supports Nyzul Isle with zero changes needed. Do not port Topaz's version -- confirmed via direct file read, not name-matching. CHECK PER PACKAGE for any future zone: this file is shared/global to the whole Assault system, not per-zone, so it only needs checking once, not once per package.

method_renames._readme: Confirmed Lua METHOD-NAME differences (not tpz.* namespace substitutions) -- same entity, same purpose, different binding name between Topaz and DSP. Safe for the converter to auto-apply via a colon-call regex (':<old>(' -> ':<new>('), confirmed by reading the real C++ binding in both codebases.

getCharVar.evidence: DSP's getVar/setVar are PC-only (asserts objtype==TYPE_PC) and persist to a char_vars SQL table -- same semantics as Topaz's getCharVar/setCharVar, just renamed. Rule: player:getCharVar(x) -> player:getVar(x).

setCharVar.evidence: see getCharVar -- same pairing. Rule: player:setCharVar(x, v) -> player:setVar(x, v).

PrintToPlayer.evidence: Case-only difference -- DSP registers lowercase printToPlayer, not PrintToPlayer. Found auditing assault_gm_debug_tools (all 10 GM command files used the Topaz-style capital-P spelling).

goToEntity.source: src/map/lua/lua_base_entity.cpp:20649 (SOL_REGISTER), function itself defined at line 4280
goToEntity.evidence: Case-only difference (capital T -> lowercase t in "to") -- DSP registers gotoEntity, not goToEntity. Found in gotoinstid.lua.

untargetable.evidence: Not a case difference -- Topaz's bare untargetable(bool) toggle does not exist in DSP at all under any casing; the real binding is setUntargetable(bool), same single-bool-arg signature. Found in navdebug.lua.

addCharVar.source: src/map/lua/lua_base_entity.cpp:735 (SOL_REGISTER at :20504), signature void incrementCharVar(const std::string& varName, int32 value)
addCharVar.evidence: addCharVar (invented -- no such binding exists anywhere in lua_base_entity.cpp) was used exclusively as v:addCharVar("AssaultsCompleted", 1) in every zone Rune_of_Release.lua, i.e. a true increment-by-value call. incrementCharVar has the identical (varName, value) signature and real increment semantics (charutils::IncrementCharVar) -- exact match, not just a plausible substitute. Found auditing the 5 zone packages (remaining_7_packages_binding_audit_2026-09-13.md).

getShortID.evidence: getShortID (invented -- no such binding exists anywhere in lua_base_entity.cpp) was used exclusively as the single argument to :engage(...) (e.g. mob:engage(target:getShortID())). engage(uint16 requestedTarget) (src/map/lua/lua_base_entity.cpp:13063) expects exactly the targid getTargID() returns -- confirmed matching signature/purpose, not a guess. Found across 4 of 5 zone packages auditing the 5 zone packages (remaining_7_packages_binding_audit_2026-09-13.md).

setName.source: src/map/lua/lua_base_entity.cpp:6090 (SOL_REGISTER at :20715), signature void renameEntity(const std::string& newName, const sol::object& arg2=silent)
setName.evidence: setName (invented -- no such binding exists anywhere in lua_base_entity.cpp) was used as a single-arg call (npc:setName(realName)). renameEntity(newName) matches that exact call shape (the second arg is an optional silent-log bool, unused either way) and its real doc example is literally mob:renameEntity("NewName"). Also sets updatemask |= UPDATE_NAME, same queued-broadcast-not-immediate semantics the calling file already had to work around for Topaz's setName() -- found in periqia's Hunched_Figure.lua (remaining_7_packages_binding_audit_2026-09-13.md).

setAnimationSub.evidence: setAnimationSub/getAnimationSub (LandSandBoat-shaped split accessor names, checked against the wrong codebase in an earlier pass) do not exist in old-dsp-reference -- real binding is a single unified AnimationSub(value) getter/setter (get when called with no args, set when called with one), same pattern as the already-fixed speed(). AnimationSub(value) also pushes a real CCharUpdatePacket/CEntityUpdatePacket itself on every set, making a separate forceRespawn()/updateToEntireZone() broadcast call unnecessary after it. Found via backport_binding_audit.py 2026-09-13.

getAnimationSub.evidence: Same unified accessor as setAnimationSub above -- AnimationSub() with no args returns the current value.

delEffectFlag.evidence: delEffectFlag is Topaz's own convenience alias for the same real setFlag/unsetFlag pair (confirmed: Topaz's own lua_statuseffect.cpp registers "delEffectFlag" -> CLuaStatusEffect::unsetFlag directly) -- old-dsp-reference never had the alias, only the real unsetFlag name. Found via backport_binding_audit.py 2026-09-13, nyzul_isle_investigation package.

isEngaged.evidence: Did not exist as a Lua binding in old-dsp-reference at all (confirmed absent) -- real underlying C++ capability (CAIContainer::IsEngaged(), PAI declared on every CBaseEntity) already existed, just never exposed. Added as a new C++ binding, same name as Topaz's own isEngaged() (lua_baseentity.cpp:8880) -- no Lua-side rename needed once compiled. See dsp-engine-changes/isengaged/README.md.

forceRespawn.evidence: Did not exist in old-dsp-reference at all (confirmed absent) -- ported directly using pieces already real and in-use in this codebase (CEntityUpdatePacket/ENTITY_DESPAWN/ENTITY_SPAWN/UPDATE_ALL_MOB/PAI->QueueAction, same pattern this file's own hideNPC() already uses). per_zone_id_file_conventions._readme: CRITICAL: the id-constants file name AND shape is NOT uniform across zones in this DSP snapshot -- always check what already exists for a given zone before assuming a convention. Two known shapes so far:

shape_A_nested_table.shape: a single global table named after the zone (e.g. `NyzulIsle = { text = {...}, mobs = {...}, npcs = {...} }`), closely matching Topaz's own IDs.lua shape -- just a bare global instead of `local ID = require(...)`
shape_A_nested_table.conversion_rule: keep the filename `IDs.lua` and the zone-table name; change `local ID = require("scripts/zones/X/IDs")` to `require("scripts/zones/X/IDs")` (no local assignment) and `ID.text.X`/`ID.npc.X`/`ID.mob[N].X` to `ZoneTable.text.X`/`ZoneTable.npcs.X`/`ZoneTable.mobs[N].X` (note: DSP pluralizes to `mobs`/`npcs`, Topaz uses singular `mob`/`npc` -- check this per zone too).

shape_B_flat_bare_globals.shape: flat bare global constants, no wrapping table at all (e.g. `REQUIRES_A_PET = 215;`)
shape_B_flat_bare_globals.conversion_rule: keep the filename `TextIDs.lua`; change `local ID = require("scripts/zones/X/IDs")` to `require("scripts/zones/X/TextIDs")`; change every `ID.text.X` to bare `X`. This shape has NO established convention for npc/mob id tables (only text ids were found) -- when a zone's Topaz IDs.lua has real npc/mob id tables and DSP's TextIDs.lua doesn't, either add them as new bare globals in TextIDs.lua (matching this shape) or hardcode the numeric literal at each call site (matching how DSP's own real scripts for that zone already do it) -- check the zone's own existing scripts for the established local precedent before choosing.

shape_C_zones_table_global.example_zones: Periqia, Leujaoam_Sanctum, Mamool_Ja_Training_Grounds, Lebros_Cavern, Ilrusi_Atoll, Aht_Urhgan_Whitegate, Bhaflau_Thickets, Caedarva_Mire (Al_Zahbi/Nashmau/Wajaom_Woodlands/Mount_Zhayolm structurally identical by inspection of their IDs.lua header, not each individually read line-by-line)
shape_C_zones_table_global.discovered: 2026-09-13, during the 7-new-package DSP conversion pass -- neither shape_A nor shape_B (both from the Nyzul package, 2026-09-xx) matched this DSP snapshot's CURRENT IDs.lua for any of these zones, including Aht_Urhgan_Whitegate itself -- shape_B (TextIDs.lua) is STALE for Whitegate in this checkout: it now has a real IDs.lua in shape_C, no TextIDs.lua at all. This snapshot has evolved since the Nyzul package; shape_B may be entirely obsolete now -- re-verify before trusting it for any zone.
shape_C_zones_table_global.shape: `zones = zones or {}` then `zones[xi.zone.<ZONE>] = { text = {...}, mob = {...}, npc = {...} }`, file ends with `return zones[xi.zone.<ZONE>]`. Field names are SINGULAR (`mob`/`npc`, not `mobs`/`npcs`) -- same spelling as Topaz's own IDs.lua. Some npc (and occasionally mob, see Lebros_Cavern's WAMOURA_OFFSET) entries resolve via `GetFirstID('Name')`/`GetTableOfIDs('Name')` instead of a hardcoded numeric literal (Ilrusi_Atoll is the only zone checked that hardcodes every value instead).
shape_C_zones_table_global.real_consumption_pattern: DSP's own instance/mob/npc scripts in these zones read it back via `local ID = zones[xi.zone.<ZONE>]` (a global table lookup, NOT `require(...)`) -- confirmed by reading scripts/zones/Mamool_Ja_Training_Grounds/instances/preemptive_strike.lua, imperial_agent_rescue.lua, Mamool_Ja_Warder.lua, Dilapidated_Gate.lua, globals/zoneUtil.lua; scripts/zones/Ilrusi_Atoll/npcs/Cursed_Chest.lua, mobs/Carrion_{Toad,Slime,Leech,Crab}.lua, instances/{golden_salvage,extermination}.lua; scripts/zones/Lebros_Cavern/mobs/Qiqirn_{Volcanist,Mine,Ceramist}.lua, mobs/Brittle_Rock.lua, instances/{wamoura_farm_raid,troll_fugitives,excavation_duty}.lua; scripts/zones/Periqia/instances/{shades_of_vengeance,seagull_grounded,requiem}.lua -- all 22 real files use `local ID = zones[xi.zone.X]`, zero use require().
shape_C_zones_table_global.conversion_rule: keep filename IDs.lua. Rewrite ONLY the require line: `local ID = require("scripts/zones/X/IDs")` -> `local ID = zones[xi.zone.X]` (bare table lookup, uppercase zone enum, no require/local-module semantics). Every `ID.text.X`/`ID.mob[N].X`/`ID.mob.X`/`ID.npc.X` call site is UNCHANGED -- Topaz's own singular shape already matches DSP's shape_C exactly, so LESS conversion work is needed here than shape_A's Nyzul case, not more. Implemented in backport_lua_convert.py as id_shape='zones_table' (zone_table param repurposed to carry the bare xi.zone.* enum name, e.g. 'PERIQIA') -- _convert_id_references() is a no-op for this shape, _convert_id_requires_zones_table() handles the require rewrite, and _flag_unhandled()'s 'unconverted ID.*' check is suppressed for this shape since the lack of conversion is correct, not a gap.

per_zone_id_file_conventions.how_to_check_a_new_zone: 1) does scripts/zones/<Zone>/IDs.lua or TextIDs.lua (or neither) already exist in DSP? 2) if it exists, read it in FULL (not head/tail) -- is it a wrapping table under a DIFFERENT name than the zone (shape A), flat bare globals (shape B), or `zones[xi.zone.X]={...}` read back as `local ID = zones[xi.zone.X]` (shape C)? shape C has been the answer for every zone checked as of 2026-09-13 (10 zones across 2 packages) -- treat it as the current default expectation, and re-verify shape A/B claims from the Nyzul package before relying on them, since this snapshot visibly evolved since then (Whitegate itself moved off shape B). 3) if NEITHER file exists, this is a genuinely new zone for DSP -- pick shape C as the default now (supersedes the old shape-A-default guidance), since it's both the closer match to Topaz's own structure AND the actually-observed current convention.

script_shape._readme: The file-level Lua convention differs from Topaz's current style across the whole DSP snapshot, not per-zone.
script_shape.conversion_rule: for every `entity.<hook> = function(<args>) <body> end` block, emit `function <hook>(<args>) <body> end` at the same position; drop the `local entity = {}` line and the trailing `return entity` line. Preserve all other code (comments, local functions, requires) verbatim in position.
script_shape.id_require_rule: `local ID = require("scripts/zones/X/IDs")` -> `require("scripts/zones/X/<filename per per_zone_id_file_conventions>")` with no local assignment (DSP's convention loads these as side-effecting global-defining files, not modules that return a table to capture).
